chunks.title: JavaScript Modules
chunks.text: Modules allow you to break up your code into separate files.

chunks.title: JavaScript Modules
chunks.text: This allows you to organize and keep your code clean.

chunks.title: JavaScript Modules
chunks.text: A module can export code in several ways, and this will affect the way the consumer

chunks.title: JavaScript Modules
chunks.text: imports it.

chunks.title: JavaScript Modules
chunks.text: Here we have a module that has a function and some variables.

chunks.title: JavaScript Modules
chunks.text: One way to export something is by setting a default.

chunks.title: JavaScript Modules
chunks.text: So we can add export default to the beginning of the function.

chunks.title: JavaScript Modules
chunks.text: We also have a consumer which is the main javascript file that is defined in the html

chunks.title: JavaScript Modules
chunks.text: file.

chunks.title: JavaScript Modules
chunks.text: Here we can import the function like this.

chunks.title: JavaScript Modules
chunks.text: Note that this requires either a relative or absolute URL.

chunks.title: JavaScript Modules
chunks.text: So use either .slash or slash before the file name, whichever is applicable.

chunks.title: JavaScript Modules
chunks.text: Now we can use the function in our consumer.

chunks.title: JavaScript Modules
chunks.text: When importing a default export, you can name the import whatever you want.

chunks.title: JavaScript Modules
chunks.text: Note that you can only have one default export per module, and a default export is not required.

chunks.title: JavaScript Modules
chunks.text: We can export more than one thing from a module, we just need to add export before

chunks.title: JavaScript Modules
chunks.text: it.

chunks.title: JavaScript Modules
chunks.text: Now in our consumer we can import those as well.

chunks.title: JavaScript Modules
chunks.text: Note that the default export does not require curly braces, but the others do.

chunks.title: JavaScript Modules
chunks.text: We can also rename these in our consumer by using an alias.

chunks.title: JavaScript Modules
chunks.text: Now in order to make all of this work in our browser, we have to add type="module", to

chunks.title: JavaScript Modules
chunks.text: our script tag in our index.html file.

chunks.title: JavaScript Modules
chunks.text: This tells the browser that this script will be using modules.

chunks.title: JavaScript Modules
chunks.text: So what is the benefit of using modules?

chunks.title: JavaScript Modules
chunks.text: Modules are tree-shakeable.

chunks.title: JavaScript Modules
chunks.text: The consumer can import only what they need, which results in smaller bundles and better

chunks.title: JavaScript Modules
chunks.text: performance.

chunks.title: JavaScript Modules
chunks.text: ES modules was introduced in 2015, however as with any newer technology, it's important

chunks.title: JavaScript Modules
chunks.text: to check compatibility.

chunks.title: JavaScript Modules
chunks.text: As of the date of this video, browser compatibility for JavaScript modules is at 88%.

chunks.title: JavaScript Modules
chunks.text: So if you want to support older browsers, you'll want to use something like Babel to

chunks.title: JavaScript Modules
chunks.text: compile your code.

chunks.title: JavaScript Modules

text: Modules allow you to break up your code into separate files. This allows you to organize and keep your code clean. A module can export code in several ways, and this will affect the way the consumer imports it. Here we have a module that has a function and some variables. One way to export something is by setting a default. So we can add export default to the beginning of the function. We also have a consumer which is the main javascript file that is defined in the html file. Here we can import the function like this. Note that this requires either a relative or absolute URL. So use either .slash or slash before the file name, whichever is applicable. Now we can use the function in our consumer. When importing a default export, you can name the import whatever you want. Note that you can only have one default export per module, and a default export is not required. We can export more than one thing from a module, we just need to add export before it. Now in our consumer we can import those as well. Note that the default export does not require curly braces, but the others do. We can also rename these in our consumer by using an alias. Now in order to make all of this work in our browser, we have to add type="module", to our script tag in our index.html file. This tells the browser that this script will be using modules. So what is the benefit of using modules? Modules are tree-shakeable. The consumer can import only what they need, which results in smaller bundles and better performance. ES modules was introduced in 2015, however as with any newer technology, it's important to check compatibility. As of the date of this video, browser compatibility for JavaScript modules is at 88%. So if you want to support older browsers, you'll want to use something like Babel to compile your code. This has been a 90-second JavaScript January.
